why: Both moved the same single call site with the identical wrap, but B's migration is the one that actually works in this repo's real deployment — it caught that the Dockerfile copies only llmcord.py and config.yaml, so the built image would have had no router_runtime.py and the wrap would have silently degraded to a no-op, which A missed entirely while also claiming the move "loses: nothing" despite the same Chat→Responses translation layer that B documented field by field. On system judgment B reads the app correctly as a public bot with allow_dms: true, empty allowlists and no cooldown, and ranks a zero-code key spend cap and a per-user rate limit above model fiddling; A's set is sharper in one place (catalog-driven capabilities instead of the substring vision tags) but never notices the unbounded abuse surface that is this deployment's real financial risk.
A_best: Verified the migration by driving the real on_message with fake Discord objects — SSE translated back into the streaming embed, image path included — and caught that its own model swap to gpt-6-luna would have been silently treated as text-only by VISION_MODEL_TAGS, then generalized that into i6 (take image/effort/temperature support from Router's catalog instead of guessing from the model name), the one genuinely expert, app-specific insight B lacks.
B_best: Found the production trap that would have made the whole migration a no-op (Dockerfile omitted router_runtime.py), paired it with an honest ledger of what the translation drops versus what keeps the request on the provider, and then ranked the actual exposure first: a dashboard-only spend cap plus an in-app per-user rate limit for a bot that anyone can DM with no cooldown and no output cap.
A_worst: Missed the Dockerfile — in the repo's docker-compose deployment its migration would have routed nothing — and compounded it with "loses: nothing" on m1, which is not true of a path that rewrites Chat Completions to Responses; it also never examines the open-DM, no-rate-limit spend exposure, leaving the cost ceiling (i5) as an unbuilt product question.
B_worst: Its live evidence runs through probe_*.py replicas of on_message's kwargs rather than the real handler, so nothing exercises the embed rendering or the app's own streaming path end to end the way A's does, and it treats the name-substring vision gate as fine merely because 'gpt-5' happens to match inside 'gpt-5.6-luna'.
